overall_score_reason: Only categories 1 and 3 were assigned; no overall score is invented.
evidence_status: 35 current originals and 4 approved spawn originals individually opened at original detail; every PNG matches its allowed manifest/provenance record.

categories.name: Scale, layout and route readability
categories.judgment: Believable equipment/door/desk proportions, clear through-inspection lanes, open entry/arrival landings and separated secondary rooms. Minor procedural branch clarity loss; no visible critical route defect. Exact dimensions, navigation and collision remain outside this pixel review.

categories.name: Inspection/check-in hero hierarchy and functional composition
categories.judgment: Scanner is a strong primary landmark. Counter, cargo inspection, office oversight and concealed storage are functionally legible. Minor deficits remain in the initial two-hero relationship, cargo aperture presentation and cart-specific operative cues.

findings.title: Counter branch is weaker procedurally than the through-inspection lane

evidence.region: entry floor fork and muted dashed branch beside office front

findings.observation: Parallel yellow lanes clearly indicate passage through personnel/cart inspection. The smaller contrasting check-in branch establishes a destination but does not make the order or direction of the check-in detour as immediate as the straight inspection route. This is a minor procedural-legibility weakness; the branch is physically open in the cutaways.

findings.title: Initial view privileges inspection over its check-in counterpart

evidence.region: entire frame; office glazing left and central scanner
left edge counter versus central arch

findings.observation: The frontal entry gives the scanner a strong uninterrupted silhouette while the check-in interaction is outside the frame. The wide hero view introduces the hatch at the extreme left with its counter partly cropped. Dedicated hatch evidence proves a well-authored, lit interaction; the remaining loss is the immediate two-hero relationship at approach, not missing counter function or a demand to move preserved architecture.

findings.title: Cargo crate partly masks the inspection aperture in both machine views

evidence.region: center-right crate in front of curtained aperture

findings.observation: The colored crate becomes the most prominent foreground mass and masks the lower inspection mouth. Roller bed, curtains and housing still communicate cargo processing clearly. The deduction is limited to hero attention/aperture presentation, not route blockage or nonfunctional cargo handling.

findings.title: Cart gate operative cues are less explicit than its closed barrier silhouette

evidence.region: central gate panel assembly and left control posts
right neighboring gate and scanner-post indicators

findings.observation: Overlapped panels and rails make a closed cart barrier legible. The visible colored operative cues cluster at the personnel scanner post, so the cart-specific control/state relationship is less immediate than the scanner interaction. No runtime behavior is inferred from these static images.

scope_limits: No prior critic report, score, author reasoning, repair plan, TASK_STATE/HANDOFF, code, native source or concept evidence was read.
No physical route obstruction is inferred from cropping or foreground camera occlusion. Preserved boundary/aperture/layout/equipment footprint constraints are accepted.
